reality_delta: The first post-review concern has been concretely resolved. Cap override is no longer only metadata: runtime/bin/redcap advisory-stop override writes a bounded, expiring, reason-bearing marker; codex-hook.py loads that marker in print_advisory_stop and emits continue=true when it is valid; both the standalone advisory-stop check and the codex-hook self-check now include end-to-end scenarios that prove first Stop blocks and a second Stop continues after the override marker is written. The contract documents the override command and updated residual risks. The Stop timeout was raised to 300 seconds. Hook-coverage-check, host-hook-audit, enforcement-check, and the advisory-stop e2e regression all passed in this review. The remaining gaps are accepted known limits rather than unaddressed concerns.
main_concern: No blocking concern remains. The strongest residual issue is that full runtime/bin/redcap check still runs inside the Stop hot path, which keeps closeout latency higher than a no-Stop design and retains a recursion surface if a check failure becomes coupled to Stop state. This is explicitly acknowledged as a residual risk and the timeout was raised, but it is not a regression from the user's authorized design.
top_risks: Full runtime/bin/redcap check invoked from Stop creates closeout latency and a theoretical recursion surface; the 300s timeout mitigates but does not eliminate this.
The override marker requires the caller to supply the exact session_id and turn_id; Cap must map these from the Stop context, which is possible but not ergonomically exposed in the block JSON.
A real Codex-fired Stop event has not yet been observed; the deployment proof relies on adapter self-check until the host reloads the hook config and a live closeout occurs.
missing_evidence: A real host-fired Stop marker recorded after Codex reloads the new hook config, proving the deployed event fires in production.
A timing baseline for the full redcap check invocation from Stop under realistic load, to validate the 300s budget.
A test that exercises the runtime/bin/redcap advisory-stop override CLI command itself, not only the underlying marker writer.
minimum_fix: No fix is required to satisfy the current user intent. As a forward recommendation, monitor actual Stop closeout latency after Codex restart; if the full redcap check invocation exceeds the operational budget, move it out of the Stop hot path into a pre-closeout or background check while keeping the deterministic guards (turn-action, terminal-goal, final-claim, scan-conclusion, human-output) in Stop.

anti_loop_signal.reason: The code enforces max_rounds per session_id+turn_id, replaces repeated constraints with a bounded max-correction-rounds message, requires original_task_excerpt and recovery_focus_anchor, sets do_not_answer_the_hook=true, and validates override markers with expiry and minimum reason length. These guards are exercised by both the e2e regression and the codex-hook self-check.
